stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the Sharon Statement (Young Americans for Freedom, September 1960). Account drawn from the grounding books (Barron's Ch. 10, Topic 8.14; 5 Steps Ch. 28; Princeton Ch. 12).
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of the Sharon Statement, adopted by Young Americans for Freedom in September 1960 at Sharon, Connecticut. The statement said that free markets and personal freedom go together, that government should be limited to protecting freedom and keeping order, and that the United States must stand firmly against communism.

stem: The statement best shows which of the following about the conservative movement in 1960?

options.text: Conservatives agreed with liberals in 1960 that government should stay large.
options.misconception: The statement calls for limited government. Background: That limited-government program was the opposite of the liberal program of the 1960s.

options.text: Conservatives were already joining free-market ideas, limited government, and anti-communism into one program.
The conservative movement began only after Ronald Reagan won the presidency in 1980.
options.misconception: The statement dates from 1960, twenty years before Reagan's election.

options.text: Young conservatives rejected anti-communism and welcomed Soviet power in America instead.
options.misconception: The statement says the United States must stand firmly against communism.

rationales.A: The statement calls for limited government. Background: That limited-government program was the opposite of the liberal program of the 1960s.
rationales.B: The statement joins all three in one place: free markets, limited government, and standing against communism.
rationales.C: Background: The statement dates from 1960, twenty years before Reagan's election in 1980.
rationales.D: The statement says the United States must stand firmly against communism.
rationales.general:
1. Count the ideas in the statement: free markets, limited government, and anti-communism.
2. All three appear in one short statement from 1960, written by young conservatives.
3. Background: That combination became the core of the New Right, so the movement was already taking shape in 1960.
Remember: When a short document packs several ideas together, that packing is the point.
